input.body:
label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the "weekly" branch unconditionally adds 7 days to `from`, unlike the "daily" branch which only rolls forward a day if the computed run time has already passed today. This means a weekly schedule created before `RUN_HOUR_UTC` (06:00 UTC) on its chosen day skips that day's run entirely and waits a full week before the first export, which matches both reports (created at 05:40 UTC and the earlier August case). The weekly case needs the same "next <= from" check the daily case has, so the first run can happen on the creation day when the run hour hasn't passed yet.

input.title: Fix weekly/monthly scheduled exports skipping their first run
input.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

`nextRunAt` only checks `if (next <= from)` before advancing for the "daily" cadence; the "weekly" and "monthly" branches unconditionally add 7 days / move to next month's 1st, regardless of whether the computed run time (today at RUN_HOUR_UTC) is still in the future relative to `from`.

This means a weekly (or monthly) schedule created earlier in the day than RUN_HOUR_UTC gets its very first run skipped: `next` lands later today, which is a valid future run time, but the code still jumps a full week/month ahead. A schedule created after RUN_HOUR_UTC happens to behave correctly, which matches the reporter's observation that an export created at 09:00 worked while one created at 05:40 UTC (before the 06:00 run hour) silently missed its first send.

Proposed fix: apply the same `if (next <= from)` guard to the "weekly" and "monthly" cases before advancing, so the first run only skips ahead when the computed time has already passed, consistent with the "daily" branch.
